articleTitle: Oral Cancer: Signs, Diagnosis, and Treatment Basics

linkedin.content:
Many dismiss a persistent mouth ulcer as a minor inconvenience. But if a sore on your lip or in your mouth hasn't healed after 2-3 weeks, it's important to get it checked by a doctor or dentist.

Oral cancer, which can affect the lips, tongue, gums, and lining of the mouth, is often linked to tobacco use, especially in the form of gutka, paan masala, khaini, bidi, and cigarettes. Other risk factors include heavy alcohol use and prolonged sun exposure.

Warning signs can include a lump or thickening in the mouth, white or red patches, bleeding, pain, numbness, changes in voice, loose teeth, or difficulty chewing or swallowing. While these symptoms may have other causes, persistent issues should always be evaluated by a doctor. Early detection is key.

If you notice any of these signs, or if you use tobacco in any form, please speak with your doctor or dentist. They can assess your risk and discuss screening options. In India, the Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) scheme may cover much of the cost of oral cancer treatment for eligible families.

twitter.content:
1/ Noticed a mouth sore that just won't heal, even after a few weeks? It's easy to ignore, but don't. A persistent sore needs a check-up.

2/ Oral cancer can show up as a sore, lump, or white/red patch in your mouth. These aren't *always* cancer, but if they stick around for 2-3 weeks, get them checked by a doctor or dentist.

3/ Gutka, paan masala, khaini, bidi, and cigarettes increase your risk of oral cancer. If you use tobacco, talk to a doctor about quitting and getting screened.

4/ Regular dental visits can catch early signs of oral cancer, even if you don't notice symptoms. Aim for a check-up every 6-12 months, especially if you use tobacco.

5/ Worried about costs? Many cancer treatments, including oral cancer, are covered under Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) for eligible families. Ask the hospital's PMJAY desk.

6/ Got questions about mouth sores or lumps? A doctor or dentist can help. Don't delay seeking advice. Learn more about oral cancer: https://suchitracancercare.org/cancer-type/oral-cancer/

youtube_short.content:
Ever bitten your cheek and had a sore that just won't quit? Most oral cancers in India start with something like that – a mouth sore people ignore for too long. Let's talk about what to watch for.

First, oral cancer isn't just one thing. It can show up on your lips, tongue, gums, even the roof of your mouth. Most of the time, it starts in the flat cells lining your mouth. These cells can form white patches that don't rub off.

Second, tobacco is a HUGE risk. We’re talking gutka, paan masala, khaini, bidi, cigarettes – all of it. These things seriously increase your chances of getting oral cancer. It's also more likely if you drink alcohol heavily or spend a lot of time in the sun.

Third, know the warning signs. A sore that won't heal, a lump, a white or red patch, bleeding, numbness, loose teeth, trouble swallowing, even a change in your voice could be a sign. These things don't always mean cancer, but if they last for more than two or three weeks, get them checked.

So, what should you do? If you notice any of these signs that last more than a couple of weeks, don't wait. See a doctor or dentist. Regular dental checkups are also a good idea, especially if you use tobacco. Early detection makes a big difference.
